yaml.label: A complete configuration
yaml.input:
# Configuration for a local tool
service: ParseCove
enabled: true
owner:
  id: "001"
  name: Ada
yaml.note: The comment and presentation are discarded; supported data values remain.

yaml.label: yes is a string in this schema
yaml.note: YAML 1.2 core resolves true as a boolean; yes stays a string. A YAML 1.1 parser may differ.

yaml.label: Identifiers, dates and null
yaml.note: The quoted ID keeps its zeroes. Dates stay strings with the core schema used here.

yaml.label: An alias becomes repeated values
yaml.note: JSON represents the two arrays as values; it has no anchor syntax or shared-reference identity.

yaml.label: Duplicate keys are rejected
yaml.note: Two values for the same key are ambiguous. This converter rejects the mapping rather than silently keeping one.

yaml.label: A non-string key needs attention
yaml.note: JSON object keys must be strings. Quote the YAML key explicitly when its text is intended.

json.label: A string containing a JSON document
json.note: One parse gives JSON text held in a string. Only parse that text again if your data contract expects an object.

json.label: One more string layer
json.note: The result is still a complete JSON string literal. Inspect one known layer at a time; do not loop until a value changes type.

json.label: An object is already an object
json.note: The first parse already returns an object. JSON.parse is not a general operation to apply repeatedly to any value.

json.label: Backslashes can be real data
json.note: The escaped source represents a path and a newline. Global backslash deletion would change or corrupt those values.

json.label: A numeric-looking string
json.note: This string is an identifier, not another document. Preserve its type and leading zeros.

json.label: One field contains JSON text
json.note: The document is an object; payload is a string by design. Decode only that known field when its contract says it holds JSON.

json.label: A raw newline inside quotes
json.note: An unescaped line feed inside a JSON string is invalid. Encode the newline as a backslash-n sequence in the source.
